summary: Intermittent embedding delivery-order instability causing rerank candidate mismatch and tail queueing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent reorder of embeddings at the rerank step: embeddings arrive with non-monotonic delivery-order IDs which causes candidate misalignment (scores mapped to wrong documents) and short bursts of rerank queueing and tail latency. Impact: Partial search results are incorrectly ranked for some queries (approx 0.5-2% of requests for this customer) and occasional 503s during bursts. Environment: enterprise customer on dedicated capacity in us-east with custom embed-ingest proxy in front of Redwood ingest API. Occurred after embed-ingest proxy upgrade on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Quality: incorrect top-k for affected requests, customer-visible regressions in search results.
- Latency: rerank tail latency spikes to 1.8s (baseline 120ms) and temporary queueing causing 503s.

Customer-provided example IDs and timestamps attached in logs field below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's ingest flow that batches 32 documents and sends embeddings via the ingest proxy with per-embed sequence IDs (seq_id header)
2) Trigger a backfill that concurrently sends multiple batches (parallel pipeline = 4) to reproduce high fan-in
3) Observe reranker results via customer-facing route /v1/rerank and correlate embed seq_id to candidate IDs in response metadata
4) Compare embed seq_id ordering at ingest proxy vs order observed at reranker (use request_id trace-id)
logs: 2026-03-09T22:14:08Z request_id=abc123 ingest_proxy: queued batch id=b-871 seq_ids=[1001,1002,1003,...]
2026-03-09T22:14:09Z reranker: candidate_map_mismatch request_id=abc123 top1_id=doc_1001 expected_top1=doc_1003 score_diff=0.27
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah (Support): Opened ticket after customer provided failed example traces and a sample backfill payload. Customer expects strict ordering preservation for seq_id across ingest path.

2026-03-10 Mei Chen (SRE): Verified request traces show reorder between ingest-proxy and serving-router. Hypothesis: ingest proxy uses concurrent HTTP/2 multiplexing and an async packer which drops original ordering header during internal rewrite.

2026-03-11 Daniel Ortega (Eng - Embeddings): Reproduced locally with the customer's proxy sample; found an aggressive concurrency routine in the proxy packer that merges packets out-of-order when two goroutines write to the same upstream stream. Adding a per-batch mutex preserves order at cost of small throughput drop.
2026-03-11 Customer (ClauseIQ - Emma Ramos): Confirmed problem frequency reduced when we limited parallel backfill pipelines to 1. Customer can accept temporary throttling while we patch upstream.
2026-03-12 Daniel Ortega (Eng): Patch ready (embed-proxy: fix-ordering-2841) to serialize batch writes and to add sequence_id validation in the proxy. Rolling to staging now.
2026-03-12 Support (Priya Shah): Notified customer of planned mitigation rollout and provided rollback plan.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: pattern of reorders correlates with high parallelism in customer backfill and with proxy version 2.8.3 deployed 2026-03-09.
Trace analysis: trace-id abc123 shows ingest_proxy wrote batch then internal serving-router saw packets in different order - the reorder appears before the shard assignment step.
Hypothesis 1: embed-ingest-proxy packer is non-deterministic under concurrent writes (confirmed by local repro).
Hypothesis 2: downstream shard router and reranker assume stable per-batch ordering when reconstructing candidate arrays; they do not currently validate sequence headers except in debug mode.
Reproducible conditions: high fan-in backfill, packer concurrency > 2, HTTP/2 stream multiplexing enabled. Reduced when either concurrency=1 or HTTP/2 disabled.
Risk: If undetected, corrupt ordering can produce systematic but small quality degradation (wrong candidate->score mapping) which may persist into caches and reranker training sets.
Temporary mitigation tested: configure customer's proxy to disable packer parallelism (mutex) and set HTTP/2 connection pool size to 1; observed reorder count drop to 0 in 10k requests test.

Permanent fix: enqueue patch to proxy to preserve sequence_id when reconstructing upstream frames and add sequence_id assertion in ingest API to reject out-of-order batches with a 409 for easier detection.
Related areas to check: embedding-cache invalidation logic (does it assume ordering?), reranker candidate mapping code (add defensive checks), observability (add metric for seq_id gaps).
resolution:
Workaround: Instructed ClauseIQ to throttle parallel backfill to a single pipeline and applied interim config in their proxy to serialize batch writes. This eliminated reorder incidents for their ongoing backfill.
Permanent fix: Merged PR github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2841 that adds per-batch write serialization in the embed-ingest-proxy and a sequence_id validation check in the ingest API. Patch deployed to staging on 2026-03-12 and to prod-us-east on 2026-03-12 21:00 UTC with no regressions observed in smoke tests.
Customer verification: ClauseIQ confirmed rerank quality recovered and tail latency returned to baseline.
Status: Patch deployed; monitoring in place.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add unit + integration tests for ordering under concurrent packer writes (ENG-4312)
2) Add ingest API telemetry: metric embed_seq_gap and alert when gap_rate > 0.1% (SRE-210)
3) Update embed runbook to include sequence_id validation steps and remediation playbook (DOCS-128)
4) Consider adding optional server-side reordering detection to reject batches with non-monotonic seq_ids for enterprise customers (product decision)
